text.text_excerpt: For starters, let me get this out of the way...the food is outstanding! If there was a way I could only take off half a star, I would. I went with two other people, after an afternoon spent wandering the Quarter. It was hot and this restaurant was a welcome respite from the heat. The decor is simple and pleasing. The staff is friendly, delightful, accommodating and funny. We ordered several different dishes and ate it tapas style, with all of us sharing the dishes. Once you have tasted their French Fries with banana ketchup and roasted garlic mayo, you will never be able to go back to regular condiments again. I wanted to bring home a gallon! Came here a few days ago with my husband and parents for a nice evening out. This place is pretty casual, but with more upscale food. Service was great. Would have liked dimmer lighting for an evening meal, and it was quite loud. For drinks, we tried the Schroeder's sonata (a little heavier/stronger than I imagined), el grito de Dolores (light and refreshing), and coquito (awesome, rich creamy dessert beverage), and then one other creamy one with cereal on top that I can't remember the name of! Stopped by this new spot on the rainy Sunday after being cooped up at home by TS/Hurricane Barry. They only had an abbreviated menu and were out of some options. But I get it. Love the space and I had a couple of lovely pours of bubbles. The wine list is interesting and has some nice selections. And I can't wait to try some of their signature cocktails. We ordered a preservation plate and the pickled mirlitons were my favorite. My friend LOVED the hogshead cheese. The staff is great and since it's near NOAC on Decatur, parking was easypeasy.
